registration_notes.summary: ISP Group LLC (Florida LLC, Russian-national owner) is NOT barred from ordinary federal supply contracts. It must be registered and active in SAM.gov before award (most solicitations require it at offer submission).
steps: 1. EIN/TIN from IRS (must match IRS records exactly - SAM validates TIN with IRS; allow 2-5 business days for TIN match).
2. Login.gov account -> SAM.gov 'Get a Unique Entity ID' (entity validation of legal name/address; if documents are requested, validation can take 1-4+ weeks).

3. Full SAM entity registration 'All Awards' with Reps & Certs (FAR 52.204-8/52.212-3), NAICS 424690, 325998, 325180, 424910, 212390, 325120, PSC 6810/6850/6830/6640/6630/4610/9620. CAGE code is assigned by DLA during registration. Typical activation 7-10 business days after submission; realistic total 2-4 weeks for a first-time, foreign-owned registrant.
4. Notarized letter appointing Entity Administrator is no longer required for US entities, but keep corporate documents ready for validation.
5. DoD buys: PIEE (WAWF) vendor account for invoicing; DIBBS account (needs CAGE) for DLA RFQs; NECO for NAVSUP; JCP (DD 2345) only if export-controlled drawings are needed.
6. SBA: self-certify small business in SAM (size standards: 424690 = 175 employees; 325998 = 650; 212390 = 500). Optionally create profile in SBA DSBS (part of SAM).
7. Optional later: GSA MAS schedule (6-12 months), CMMC Level 1 self-assessment for DoD contracts containing DFARS 252.204-7021/7025 (basic safeguarding of FCI).
registration_notes.earliest_eligibility: If SAM registration is started on 17.11.2026 and the TIN/entity validation goes smoothly, ISP could be active around 01-08.12.2026. Therefore all deadlines before ~01.12.2026 (Albany salt 20.11, Cherry Point salt 23.11, Jacksonville dry ice 23.11, Fort Drum road salt 30.11) are realistically missed unless ISP is already registered; RFIs/sources sought (BOP 03.12, Hill AFB 30.11) can be answered without SAM. Focus: NSWC Indian Head BPA window (30.04.2027), BOP water-treatment BPA solicitation (expected 2027), next winter salt season, recurring DLA DIBBS NSN buys.
foreign_ownership_rules: Small-business status (13 CFR 121.105): a business is 'small' if it has a place of business in the US and operates primarily within the US or makes a significant contribution to the US economy - foreign citizenship of the owner does NOT disqualify it. ISP may compete for Total Small Business set-asides and unrestricted buys.
Socio-economic set-asides require US-citizen ownership: 8(a), WOSB/EDWOSB, SDVOSB/VOSB and HUBZone are NOT available to ISP (owner is a Russian national). Several opportunities found are SDVOSB-only.

FOCI (Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence, 32 CFR Part 117/NISPOM) applies only to classified contracts requiring a facility clearance - not to plain commercial supply contracts. Not relevant here.

SAM disclosures: FAR 52.204-17 (immediate and highest-level owner), 52.204-20 (predecessor), 52.209-11/52.209-5 (tax delinquency/felony), 52.204-24/25/26 (Section 889 Huawei/ZTE etc. telecom), 52.204-27 (TikTok), 52.204-23 (Kaspersky - Russian software prohibited), FAR 52.225-13 (OFAC restrictions on certain foreign purchases), DFARS 252.225-7052 / -7056. Owner nationality is disclosed through ownership data; registration must be truthful.

Sanctions: the owner and company must not be on OFAC SDN/sectoral lists; any Russian-origin goods are effectively barred (US import bans on many Russian products under EO 14068/14071 and related; Russia is not a TAA designated country; DFARS 252.225-7008/7052 etc.). Source only US-made or TAA-country goods.

Buy American (FAR 52.225-1/-2, DFARS 252.225-7001): end products must be domestic (manufactured in the US; domestic-content threshold 65% for 2024-2028, rising to 75% in 2029) unless TAA applies (above ~$174k-183k thresholds, designated countries only - not Russia/China).

Non-manufacturer rule (13 CFR 121.406): on Small Business set-aside SUPPLY contracts above the micro-purchase threshold, a dealer like ISP must furnish the product of a US small-business manufacturer, unless the contract is under $250k (simplified acquisition - NMR still generally applies but waivers are common) or SBA has an individual/class waiver for that NAICS/PSC. Imported chemicals generally cannot be offered on SB set-asides; for unrestricted buys imports are limited by Buy American.
DoD contracts increasingly include CMMC notice clauses (seen in NAVSUP RFQs) - Level 1 self-assessment in SPRS likely required.
Export-controlled technical data (JCP/DD 2345, NNPP logistics site) is generally restricted to US/Canadian entities with US-person data custodians - a foreign-owned firm may be refused access.
